children: The European Union's executive arm outlined a plan to revamp public bidding across its 27 member states that will empower them to exclude some foreign bidders under certain circumstances.

The proposals announced on Wednesday seek to make the EU's public bidding processes easier for companies to follow and boost investments. It will also allow public authorities to leave out companies from countries that don't provide reciprocal access to European firms, which could raise scrutiny for bidders from markets like China.

It is the latest move from EU officials in recent months to use the bloc's public funding toolkit to help drive demand for European companies and boost their growth and competitiveness. The commission said that public procurement makes up around 15% of the EU's overall GDP.

Under the plans, the European Commission wants to unify other pieces of legislation on procurement into one legal text to reduce their complexity and inconsistencies on how they are applied across different sectors such as transport and energy. A second proposal focuses on investments into local companies for research and development.
EU lawmakers and member states will have to negotiate on the rulebooks--officially named the Public Procurement Act and European Innovation Act - before they can come into effect.
